Convert a Timestral forecast to a fable forecast table

Source: R/fable.R
as_fable.timestral_forecast.Rd

Registered as an S3 method for fabletools::as_fable() when fabletools is loaded; call it as fabletools::as_fable(fc). The distribution column is the 21-quantile distributional::dist_quantile() distribution from the forecast. A univariate forecast uses the variate name as the response; a fable holds a single distribution column, so a multivariate forecast becomes a variate key with the response in a value column. Forecasts from ts input use the same index class (yearmonth, yearquarter, ...) as tsibble::as_tsibble() gives the ts, so they join with and score against the observed data, and fable accuracy measures and interval extraction apply. See TIMESTRAL() for using Timestral directly as a fable model.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'timestral_forecast'
as_fable(x, ...)

Arguments

x

a timestral_forecast created from indexed input (ts, zoo, xts or tsibble), so a future time index is available

...

ignored

Value

a fbl_ts forecast table

Examples

## the tiny bundled checkpoint runs offline but its forecasts are
## meaningless; use timestral_load("5M") or larger for real ones
m <- timestral_load(system.file("extdata", "tiny", package = "timestralR"))
fc <- timestral_forecast(m, AirPassengers, h = 24)
if (requireNamespace("tsibble", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("distributional", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("fabletools", quietly = TRUE))
  fabletools::as_fable(fc)
#> # A fable: 24 x 2 [1M]
#>       index           V1
#>       <mth>       <dist>
#>  1 1961 Jan quantile[21]
#>  2 1961 Feb quantile[21]
#>  3 1961 Mar quantile[21]
#>  4 1961 Apr quantile[21]
#>  5 1961 May quantile[21]
#>  6 1961 Jun quantile[21]
#>  7 1961 Jul quantile[21]
#>  8 1961 Aug quantile[21]
#>  9 1961 Sep quantile[21]
#> 10 1961 Oct quantile[21]
#> # ℹ 14 more rows
